capitals.name: Katzenelnbogen
capitals.note: 'The original Untergrafschaft ... with its capital at Katzenelnbogen in the Middle Rhine area'; the Upper County had its seat near Darmstadt. The page gives no coordinates; Katzenelnbogen lies about 19 km north-east of the Rheinfels circle.

correction.text: the Obergrafschaft round Darmstadt and the Untergrafschaft on the Middle Rhine round St. Goar and Katzenelnbogen

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Katzenelnbogen row; the lands are in Holy Roman Empire Minor States). The page says the county 'grew from the Neckar to the Moselle over nearly four centuries' and names only the Upper County 'south of the Main River around Darmstadt' and the Lower County with its capital at Katzenelnbogen; it dates no acquisition and gives no area. Drawn as the two circles the landgraviate-of-hesse dossier uses for its 1479 gain: Darmstadt 8.65E 49.87N 30 km, and St. Goar 7.71E 50.15N 14 km. Soft; the capital town lies just outside the Rhine circle and the stretch towards the Neckar and the Moselle is not drawn.

ledger.note: 1095: the counts. Infobox 'First mentioned: 1095' (Diether I the first count); the text has Diether I 'first mentioned about 1070' in a deed of Archbishop Anno II of Cologne, and 'in 1138, King Conrad III of Germany vested his grandson Henry II with the comital title'. Entered at the infobox year.

region.text: the Katzenelnbogen lands, Upper and Lower County

ledger.note: 1260: two lines. 'The county was divided in 1260 and ruled by two lines of counts.' The page does not say which lands each line took; one state is drawn throughout (the two lines kept inside it).

1479: the line dies out. 'When Philipp died in 1479, the male line of the Katzenelnbogens became extinct. The Obergrafschaft was passed to the Landgraves of Hesse' through the 1458 marriage of Henry III of Upper Hesse to Anna, Philipp's daughter (infobox end 1479; the infobox names Hesse-Marburg).

certainty.note: No acquisition is dated and no area is given; the two circles are stand-ins for the Upper and Lower County and the early extent is not known.

sources.title: County of Katzenelnbogen

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Katzenelnbogen row.

SCOPE. 1095 (infobox 'First mentioned') to 1479 (Count Philipp's death). The text of the page conflicts with the infobox: Diether I 'was first mentioned about 1070'; the comital title was vested in 1138. I used the infobox year. The 1260 partition into two lines is a rename inside one state: the page gives no lands. The War of the Katzenelnbogen Succession (1500-1557, Hesse against Nassau-Siegen) lies after the state and is not entered here.

SHAPES. Darmstadt 8.65E 49.87N 30 km and St. Goar 7.71E 50.15N 14 km, the same two circles landgraviate-of-hesse uses for its 1479 gain and (the 14 km one) landgraviate-of-hesse-rheinfels and -kassel use for 1567/1583. The page names no towns but Darmstadt (as a region), Katzenelnbogen (capital), Burg Rheinfels, Auerbach Castle and Rüsselsheim ('In 1435, Count John IV ... was building his last castle in Rüsselsheim'), and dates no acquisition. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Katzenelnbogen', 'Darmstadt' (as a place for the circle), 'Rüsselsheim', 'Auerbach'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The early extent (the Kraichgau bequest of 1138 is not described as land); (2) all acquisitions, including Darmstadt and Rheinfels (the page gives only castle-building dates); (3) the heir: the text says the Landgraves of Hesse, the infobox says Hesse-Marburg; (4) the page gives no area.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: none new.
